Donald Trump's health has been at the center of public discourse in recent months(Image: Getty Images )

Donald Trump is "genuinely unwell" but assertions that he suffers from dementia lack evidence, according to a former presidential aide. The president has faced mounting health speculation in recent months, connected to episodes of apparent memory lapses, dozing off in public and visible bruising and swelling on his body.

However, Anthony Scaramucci, who served as Trump's communications director for ten days during his first term, rejected suggestions of cognitive decline, indicating he is "unwell" in different respects. "Trump doesn't have dementia, I'll say that clearly," Scaramucci posted on X.

"He has a narcissistic personality and the normal infirmities you'd expect at 80. But he's a fairly vigorous, fairly healthy 80. Don't underestimate him," reports Daily Express UK.

The financier and broadcaster proceeded to cite Mr Trump's inflammatory public remarks as proof that he is "genuinely unwell."

"He's making statements that are nowhere near what a world leader should be saying," Scaramucci added.

Anthony Scaramucci has become increasingly critical of Trump since leaving the White House(Image: Getty Images)

"Threatening the death and destruction of an entire civilisation on social media is a war crime... Imagine any other world leader saying anything close to that.

"It would never happen in the first place and if it did, their own party would remove them within hours."

Social media users countered that the president "is very medicated and exhibits many symptoms of dementia" along with "physical decline."

Scaramucci replied: "You may be right. I am not a doctor. I am just saying don't underestimate him."

The former Trump aide was removed from the White House in 2017 after a public falling-out with colleagues, and has grown progressively more critical of the president in subsequent years.

Trump's team, however, have strongly rejected any speculation regarding his health, maintaining he remains in "perfect" condition.

Medical professionals expressed concerns over a health report issued by the administration last month, noting it appeared to lack standard detail and presented a "filtered narrative."

But communications director Steven Cheung dismissed the criticism, stating: "President Trump has publicly released more detailed information about his health than any other president in history - showing he is in excellent health."
